lines.before: A standing grant (A27, the owner, 2026-10-31) lets named outward acts run without a yes per act. **What it holds:** `.kit/autonomy.json` names each act (for example push to main, tag, release, merge, delete a merged branch, message running sessions about a release) and the conditions it must pass. Only the owner writes or changes it; a change to it, to `.claude/autonomy.mjs` or to a gate it runs is never granted. **Before each act:** `node .claude/autonomy.mjs check <act>` reads the grant from the remote's main, never the working copy, and runs the evidence itself (tests, scrub, caps, the new test failing before the fix); a failed, missing or unreadable condition means ask the owner. **Kill switch:** the file `autonomy-off` in the Claude config folder, outside every repo; while it exists every act asks. **After:** each granted act is one line in `reports/autopilot/log.md` with its proof (the SHA or URL read back from the remote) and is reported to the owner. **Never granted:** changing the grant or its gates, deleting user data, public posts, Tier 0 rule text, or anything a test or the sweep did not pass. Projects ship with no grant (A27 `none`), so every act asks; until `autonomy.mjs` exists, no grant is in force (plan kit-autopilot). Why: the owner sets the conditions once and hears after with proof, and a gate the session can edit is no gate.
lines.after: A standing grant (A27, the owner, 2026-10-31) lets named outward acts run without a yes per act. **What it holds:** `.kit/autonomy.json` names each act (for example push to main, tag, release, merge, delete a merged branch, message running sessions about a release) and the conditions it must pass. Only the owner writes or changes it; a change to it, to `.claude/autonomy.mjs` or to a gate it runs is never granted. **Before each act:** `node .claude/autonomy.mjs check <act>` reads the grant from the remote's main, never the working copy, and runs the evidence itself (tests, scrub, caps, the new test failing before the fix); a failed, missing or unreadable condition means ask the owner. **Kill switch:** the file `autonomy-off` in the Claude config folder, outside every repo; while it exists every act asks. **After:** each granted act is one line in `reports/autopilot/log.md` with its proof (the SHA or URL read back from the remote) and is reported to the owner. **Never granted:** changing the grant or its gates, deleting user data, public posts, Tier 0 rule text, or anything a test or the sweep did not pass. **No act skips a prompt:** the ledger is advisory, and only the owner can change that, when an act first reaches 10 straight hits. Projects ship with no grant (A27 `none`), so every act asks; even a project with a grant asks while the ledger is advisory (plan kit-autopilot). Why: the owner sets the conditions once and hears after with proof, and a gate the session can edit is no gate, nor is a verdict it can write.
lines.why: the owner, 2026-10-31: the streak of owner verdicts is advisory (the ledger is forgeable), so no act skips a prompt, and only the owner can change that when an act first reaches 10 straight hits
